summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need a model to internalize a specific style, format, domain vocabulary, or task behavior that cannot be reliably achieved through prompting alone, or when you want to reduce latency and cost by shrinking long prompts into learned weights. RAG is better when you need fresh, factual, or frequently changing knowledge, and prompt engineering is the cheapest first step for most tasks. In practice, teams start with prompting, add RAG for knowledge grounding, and reserve fine-tuning for consistent behavior, structured outputs, and domain adaptation at scale.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output style, tone, or structured formats (e.g. JSON schemas) that prompting cannot reliably enforce.
Fine-tune for domain adaptation when the model must internalize specialized terminology or reasoning patterns not covered in its base training.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the knowledge is factual, large-volume, or frequently updated, since retrieval avoids costly retraining.
Fine-tune to cut inference cost and latency by distilling long, repetitive system prompts into model weights for high-volume production workloads.

tools.best_for: Production fine-tuning plus optimized low-latency serving of open models

tools.name: Vertex AI
